## Overview:
The PR updates `withLock` in `src/lock.ts` to always release the acquired lock after `work()` completes, including when the work rejects or throws. It now awaits the work inside a `try/finally`, preserving the result/error contract while adding cleanup.

Specialist review may verify release behavior and error precedence when cleanup itself fails.

## Strengths:
- Ensures locks are released on both success and failure paths.
- Preserves the generic return value and async contract.
- Minimal, focused one-file change.

## Minor candidates:
none

resolvedReview.overview:
This PR fixes `withLock` in `src/lock.ts` to always release the acquired lock after `work()` settles. Previously the function returned `work()` directly and never called `release()`, so every invocation leaked its lock. The new code awaits the work inside a `try/finally`, so the lock is released on both success and rejection paths.

The change preserves the existing contracts exactly: the generic `T` return value is awaited and returned, and errors from `work()` still propagate to the caller after cleanup runs. It is a minimal, focused one-file fix that matches the PR's stated intent of refining behavior while preserving contracts.

# PR Review

**Verdict:** approve

## Overview
This PR fixes `withLock` in `src/lock.ts` to always release the acquired lock after `work()` settles. Previously the function returned `work()` directly and never called `release()`, so every invocation leaked its lock. The new code awaits the work inside a `try/finally`, so the lock is released on both success and rejection paths.

The change preserves the existing contracts exactly: the generic `T` return value is awaited and returned, and errors from `work()` still propagate to the caller after cleanup runs. It is a minimal, focused one-file fix that matches the PR's stated intent of refining behavior while preserving contracts.

## Verification
Verification was disabled: no user-level `verificationBaselines` are configured, so no trusted baseline ran against head `c2242f2cc0618705070468e003a17ce943a4d8ee`. Note that baseline execution would run PR code unsandboxed (lifecycle supervision signals only the original POSIX process group); an external sandbox or container wrapper is recommended for untrusted PRs. Review conclusions rest on the five subagent lens passes plus orchestrator source validation of the diff and surrounding file.

## Findings
No findings.

## Lane completeness
The `performance-resources` lane initially returned `partial` status with no candidate evidence; it was rerun individually with the same tool policy and completed with no findings. All other lanes (`overview`, `correctness`, `correctness-contracts`, `security-performance`) completed on the first dispatch. All requested lanes completed.

## Strengths and notes
- Lock release is now guaranteed on both success and failure paths, fixing a per-call lock leak.
- Return-value and error-propagation contracts are preserved (`await work()` in `try`, `release()` in `finally`).
- Minimal, focused change with no collateral files touched.
- Correctness: patch is sound; the only residual consideration is that a synchronously throwing `release()` in `finally` would mask the original error, but nothing in this codebase suggests `release()` can throw. Security: nothing notable. Performance: strictly improves resource behavior by eliminating lock accumulation per key.
